meta.basis: 100 internet-researched synthetic validation cases for operational Inspection Ask Defense Check workflows, based on public guidance about inspection contingencies, multiple offers, repair negotiations, seller credits, FHA/VA property standards, state inspection-period workflows, inspection-report request-builder tooling, and inspector scope limitations.
meta.warning: These cases are synthetic research translations for product validation only. They are not customer interviews, legal advice, lending advice, brokerage instructions, underwriting advice, or state-form instructions.

cases.sourceBasis: NAR inspection-contingency guidance and repair-negotiation articles support focusing on material defects rather than cosmetic preferences.
cases.persona: Buyer agent triaging a report before a same-day repair-addendum deadline
cases.deal: Conventional buyer has eight hours left in the inspection contingency and the seller is already irritated about price concessions.
findings: active roof leak at plumbing boot
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Lead with the leak and electrical safety item, keep cosmetics out, and ask for licensed evaluation or credit support before the deadline.

cases.sourceBasis: Multiple-offer guidance emphasizes that contingencies and repair demands affect offer strength, so post-inspection asks should be narrow and defensible.
cases.persona: Buyer agent protecting a backup-position buyer after winning a multiple-offer home
cases.deal: Seller accepted the offer over two backups and listing agent warns that a bloated inspection ask will not be entertained.
findings: missing GFCI protection at kitchen counter
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Keep the request short: furnace function and GFCI safety are defensible; cosmetic or age-only items should stay out.

cases.sourceBasis: State option-period workflows require action before the deadline, and public Texas guidance stresses written amendment paths.
cases.persona: Texas transaction coordinator monitoring option-period expiration
cases.deal: Option period ends at 5 p.m.; buyer agent uploads a 78-page report at noon and asks for a quick packet.
findings: Federal Pacific panel noted by inspector
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Use the remaining option window for the drain leak and panel risk only, with clear contractor follow-up and no maintenance clutter.

cases.sourceBasis: Colorado inspection objection forms treat unsatisfactory property conditions and resolution deadlines as formal deal checkpoints.
cases.persona: Colorado buyer agent drafting an inspection objection notice
cases.deal: Inspection objection deadline is tomorrow and buyer wants the packet grouped by objection priority.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The strongest objection package is sewer plus radon, not finish updates; confirm form handling with your agent or counsel.

cases.sourceBasis: Florida AS IS inspection-period sources describe inspection rights and negotiation leverage even when sellers are not obligated to repair.
cases.persona: Florida inspection coordinator supporting an AS IS buyer
cases.deal: AS IS inspection period expires in two days and insurance bindability is the buyer's primary concern.
findings: roof has 3 years estimated remaining life
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Frame this as roof and piping risk that may affect insurability and budget, not a general repair wishlist.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae and CFPB guidance show seller credits must fit closing-cost and disclosure rules, not informal post-close cash promises.
cases.persona: Transaction coordinator checking whether a requested credit is usable
cases.deal: First-time conventional buyer asks for a $14000 seller credit but estimated closing costs are $7200.
findings: seller offers post-close Venmo for repairs
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Ask for a lender/title-reviewed credit or price strategy tied to the failed systems; do not rely on off-closing side payments.

cases.sourceBasis: HUD FHA handbook materials emphasize safe, sound, secure property conditions and appraisal-visible repair concerns.
cases.persona: FHA-heavy buyer agent
cases.deal: FHA appraisal is next week and inspection found safety items that may be visible to the appraiser.
findings: peeling exterior paint on pre-1978 trim
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Prioritize FHA-visible safety and paint issues before appraisal instead of asking for normal wear items.

cases.sourceBasis: VA MPR guidance centers safety, sanitation, structural soundness, and access rather than buyer preference upgrades.
cases.persona: VA buyer specialist coordinating with lender and buyer
cases.deal: VA buyer loves the house but the inspector flagged access and safety items before appraisal.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Keep the ask tied to safety/access and the active leak; VA issues should be coordinated with the lender before wording the request.

cases.sourceBasis: Spectora and HomeGauge request-builder documentation shows agents need concise repair lists derived from inspection report items, not pasted full reports.
cases.persona: Team lead standardizing repair-request packets across junior agents
cases.deal: Brokerage wants every inspection ask to be client-readable and defensible before it goes to listing agents.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The packet should summarize the two material concerns and leave maintenance items as buyer awareness, not seller demands.

cases.sourceBasis: ASHI and InterNACHI standards describe general home inspections as limited visual evaluations, so inaccessible or specialist items need follow-up rather than overclaiming.
cases.persona: First-time buyer needing plain-English boundaries
cases.deal: Buyer believes the inspection guarantees every hidden system condition and wants the seller to warranty the house.
findings: attic partially inaccessible due to stored items
furnace flame observed but heat exchanger not evaluated
expectedLeadScope: HVAC specialist limitation if concern exists
expectedExclusions: home warranty demand framed as inspection defect
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The inspection supports follow-up where access or specialty scope was limited; it does not justify a whole-house warranty demand.

cases.sourceBasis: Repair-negotiation guidance recommends prioritizing major safety, structural, and system issues over cosmetic or preference items.
cases.persona: Inspection coordinator preparing a Sunday-night agent packet
cases.deal: Relo buyer is flying home tomorrow and needs a decision-ready summary before boarding.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Focus the ask on cooling performance and roof condition, then decide whether quotes or concessions are needed before travel disrupts communication.

cases.sourceBasis: Public negotiation sources distinguish seller repairs from buyer-controlled credits and warn that estimates strengthen requests.
cases.persona: Buyer agent comparing repair request versus credit
cases.deal: Seller wants to perform repairs personally; buyer prefers licensed trades and a clean credit.

panel lacks blanks at open slots
expectedLeadScope: panel safety correction by qualified electrician
expectedExclusions: seller handyman preference as proof of completion
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Ask for either documented licensed repairs before closing or a lender-approved credit; do not accept vague handyman promises for safety items.

cases.sourceBasis: NAR multiple-offer materials describe complex negotiation choices, making tone and scope important when a seller has alternatives.

cases.deal: Listing agent says the seller has a clean backup offer and will not reopen price over minor items.
expectedLeadScope: termite activity treatment and damage review
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: This should be a narrow risk-based request for structure and termites, not an adversarial list that invites the seller to move to backup.

cases.sourceBasis: CFPB Closing Disclosure guidance highlights checking that seller credits reflect the agreement at closing.

cases.deal: Inspection credit was agreed verbally but the preliminary closing disclosure does not show it.

seller credit absent from draft CD
buyer asks if they can close and settle later
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Before closing, reconcile the signed repair credit with lender/title and the Closing Disclosure; do not rely on a later side settlement.

cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Ask for disclosure or building maintenance context on the old stain, but do not overstate a hidden plumbing defect the inspection did not verify.

cases.sourceBasis: HUD/FHA sources emphasize utility-dependent system observation and lender-visible safety conditions.

cases.sourceBasis: VA MPR and repair negotiation guidance favor habitability and safety issues over ordinary upgrade requests.

cases.sourceBasis: NAR inspection and multiple-offer guidance supports balancing buyer protection with offer competitiveness.

cases.deal: Buyer wrote non-contingent-style terms in a competitive market but still has a short investigation window.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: If repair leverage is limited, use the inspection to decide whether foundation and sewer risk are acceptable rather than asking for cosmetic concessions.

cases.sourceBasis: Florida AS IS contract examples emphasize inspection-period timing and buyer decision leverage rather than guaranteed seller repairs.

expectedPacketSignals: AS IS does not erase diligence
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: AS IS may limit seller obligation, but you can still use the inspection period to negotiate or decide whether insurance and wiring risk are acceptable.

cases.sourceBasis: Colorado inspection-resolution workflow creates risk when parties miss the written settlement deadline.

cases.deal: Seller verbally agreed to sewer repair but no written resolution is signed and deadline is today.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not treat the verbal promise as resolved; get written resolution or decide whether to withdraw, terminate, or accept before the deadline.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae IPC guidance explains that seller contributions are limited by use and amount, so repair credits need lender review.

cases.deal: Buyer asks the agent to demand all 41 summary items because 'the inspector found them.'

cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Keep the response grounded in water and septic functionality; let the contract process, not the listing agent's pressure, drive the next step.

active leak and panel hazard buried on page 9

seller credit offered instead of repair

cases.sourceBasis: Multiple-offer sources highlight that seller concessions, timelines, and contingencies all affect negotiation strength.

cases.sourceBasis: Repair request tools emphasize downloadable, sendable lists with selected findings rather than every inspection note.

cases.sourceBasis: CFPB seller-credit disclosures and lender concession rules require document consistency before closing.
cases.persona: Transaction coordinator after inspection resolution
cases.deal: Seller agreed to a credit and a separate termite repair, but escrow instructions only show the repair.
findings: termite Section 1 repair in escrow instructions
buyer cash to close higher than expected
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Before signing closing documents, reconcile the missing credit against the signed addendum with escrow and lender.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection standards limit the general inspection scope; environmental, pest, sewer, and structural specialists may be needed.
cases.persona: First-time buyer confused by add-on inspections
cases.deal: Buyer asks why the inspection packet recommends sewer and pest follow-up instead of demanding seller replacement now.
expectedExclusions: immediate replacement demand without specialist evidence
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Use the general inspection to justify specialist follow-up first; stronger repair demands need pest or sewer evidence.

cases.sourceBasis: Repair negotiation articles recommend focusing on repairs that affect habitability or safety rather than upgrades.
cases.persona: Buyer agent for parents buying for a student
cases.deal: Parents want seller to replace all old appliances before closing.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The credible safety ask is anti-tip and dryer venting; appliance age alone is a preference issue if the units work.

cases.sourceBasis: Texas option-period guidance supports fast, written, deadline-aware repair decisions.
cases.persona: High-volume Texas transaction coordinator
cases.deal: Coordinator has six inspection packets in one day and needs product output to flag deadline risk.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: With nine hours left, decide whether to request extension for foundation review and include the roof leak; do not spend the window on cosmetics.

cases.sourceBasis: Florida AS IS inspection-period sources support buyer cancellation or negotiation decisions during the period, even without seller repair obligation.
cases.persona: Florida first-time buyer's agent
cases.deal: Buyer thinks AS IS means they wasted money on inspection because seller refused repairs.
findings: electrical panel brand flagged by insurer
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The inspection still matters: it gives you insurance and roof facts to negotiate, accept, or cancel within the inspection period.

cases.sourceBasis: Colorado form workflow emphasizes written objection and resolution deadlines, not informal text-message agreements.
cases.persona: Colorado buyer agent receiving seller texts
cases.deal: Seller texted that they will repair radon and sewer, but no resolution is signed.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Treat the text as a negotiation signal, not a completed resolution; get written terms before the deadline.

cases.sourceBasis: Public repair-credit guidance and lender rules support checking whether credits, price reductions, or repairs best fit the buyer's constraints.
cases.persona: Buyer agent advising a cash-poor conventional buyer
cases.deal: Buyer needs cash after closing for repairs but has limited allowable closing costs left.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: A seller credit may not create repair cash if closing costs are limited; discuss credit, price, or seller repair options around the sewer quote.

cases.sourceBasis: Reasonable repair guidance favors objective findings, estimates, and safety framing over emotional negotiation language.
cases.persona: Team lead reviewing buyer-facing tone
cases.deal: Buyer wants to accuse the seller of hiding a leak in the repair request.
findings: fresh paint near active window leak
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Use factual moisture and leak evidence, and let your agent handle disclosure questions without inflammatory wording.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection standards and scope limitations require differentiating observed defects from predictions of future failure.
cases.persona: First-time buyer worried every old system will fail
cases.deal: Buyer asks for replacement of every component older than 15 years.
findings: roof old with no active leak
expectedExclusions: boiler replacement solely due to age
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Negotiate active seepage and handrail safety; treat old functional systems as budgeting risk unless a specialist documents failure.

cases.sourceBasis: NAR multiple-offer guidance includes seller strategy and counteroffer risks, which matter when a buyer asks after beating competitors.
cases.persona: Buyer agent whose client won against eleven offers
cases.deal: Buyer kept inspection contingency but promised not to nickel-and-dime in cover letter.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Honor the no-nickel-and-dime posture by asking only for the leak and electrical hazard with clear documentation.

cases.sourceBasis: Request-builder platforms allow monetary, repair, replacement, or custom requests, requiring product judgment about correct remedy signals.
cases.persona: Inspection coordinator choosing request type
cases.deal: Buyer asks whether each item should be repair, replacement, credit, or buyer awareness.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Use repair/replace language for the leaking water heater and smoke detector, and mark roof dollars as pending estimate.

cases.sourceBasis: FHA/HUD property-condition guidance makes appraiser-visible safety and paint issues operationally important before appraisal deadlines.
cases.persona: FHA transaction coordinator
cases.deal: Appraisal is tomorrow and the inspection packet still includes mostly cosmetic requests.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Before appraisal, prioritize the handrail and peeling paint; cosmetic items can jeopardize focus and timing.

cases.sourceBasis: VA MPR guidance and general repair negotiation support emphasizing water, sanitation, and safety issues.
cases.persona: VA relo buyer's coordinator
cases.deal: Military buyer is relocating and cannot attend reinspection; seller offers photos only.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: For remote VA buyers, request reliable proof or reinspection for plumbing and deck safety rather than accepting vague photos.

cases.sourceBasis: Public inspection and negotiation guidance recognizes that buyers can use inspection results for acceptance, renegotiation, or cancellation.
cases.persona: Buyer agent supporting a walk-away decision
cases.deal: Buyer has limited reserves and inspection reveals multiple expensive systems near failure.
findings: roof replacement recommended due to leaks
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: This is a major-systems cluster; negotiate only if seller response meaningfully addresses roof, sewer, and HVAC exposure.

cases.sourceBasis: Seller-credit and closing-disclosure sources require clear credit documentation and buyer understanding of allowable use.
cases.persona: Transaction coordinator explaining amendment wording
cases.deal: Repair amendment says 'seller to help buyer with repairs' but title asks for precise credit wording.
findings: title cannot draft from vague text
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Use precise, lender/title-approved credit language tied to the plumbing issue rather than vague repair-help wording.

cases.sourceBasis: Reasonable requests after inspection exclude upgrades and cosmetic improvements that were visible before offer.
cases.persona: Buyer agent resisting buyer remorse
cases.deal: Buyer now wants seller to pay for a pool remodel after seeing maintenance comments.
expectedLeadScope: inoperative pool heater if included system
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Ask about pool electrical safety and heater function if included; a visible plaster remodel is not an inspection defect request.

cases.sourceBasis: Team lead workflows require QA against lender, deadline, buyer-approval, and sendability risks.
cases.persona: Brokerage team lead doing final review before send
cases.deal: Agent's packet has no deadline, no credit check, and no buyer-approved wording.
findings: buyer did not approve final text
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not send until the deadline, credit capacity, and buyer-approved wording are confirmed; then lead with the roof leak.

cases.sourceBasis: State inspection workflows and repair guidance support explicit timing signals for operational users.
cases.persona: Inspection coordinator creating a calendar-driven packet
cases.deal: Inspection response deadline is tomorrow, lender appraisal is Friday, and seller response deadline is unclear.
expectedExclusions: operating HVAC service recommendation as demand
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Clarify response timing and prioritize appraisal-visible roof and handrail issues before Friday.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection standards and consumer guidance support buyer education about what a report can and cannot prove.
cases.persona: First-time buyer using product without agent present
cases.deal: Buyer uploaded only the report summary and asks for a final repair demand.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Upload the full report and photos before finalizing dollar requests; a summary alone is not enough for a defensible packet.

cases.sourceBasis: Public negotiation guidance recommends separating seller repair requests from buyer post-close maintenance planning.
cases.persona: Buyer agent creating both ask and maintenance list
cases.deal: Buyer asks for one document to send seller and another for post-close planning.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Send roof and deck safety to the seller; keep furnace service and caulk on your post-close maintenance list.

cases.sourceBasis: Multiple-offer sources and repair guidance support deal-preserving language under listing-agent counterpressure.
cases.persona: Buyer agent responding to listing agent who says 'take it or leave it'
cases.deal: Seller threatens no repairs, but buyer has a valid inspection contingency and major sewer evidence.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Respond calmly with sewer and electrical evidence and preserve your contractual options; do not engage over cosmetic items.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae and CFPB sources make it important to avoid promising that inspection credits can fund repairs outside closing.
cases.persona: Buyer agent training new agents on credit language
cases.deal: New agent wrote 'seller will pay buyer $8000 after closing for repairs' in draft response.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not use post-closing payment language; structure any roof concession through lender/title-approved terms.

cases.sourceBasis: HomeGauge and Spectora request-list sources show operational need for clean outputs that attach to forms rather than replace state forms.
cases.persona: Transaction coordinator attaching packet to state form
cases.deal: Agent asks the product to generate the official form instead of an attachment summary.
findings: inspection objection form required by brokerage
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Use the packet as a clean attachment summary for sewer and radon; your agent/brokerage should handle the official form.

cases.sourceBasis: Reasonable repair guidance prioritizes issues that are expensive, unsafe, or unknown before contract.
cases.persona: Repeat buyer using product across multiple offers
cases.deal: Buyer wants consistent triage rules after losing prior deals over long repair lists.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Apply the same rule here: lead with active leak and combustion safety, and avoid small-item bargaining.

cases.sourceBasis: NAR home inspection guidance and inspector standards support explaining that inspection results inform risk decisions, not automatic seller obligations.
cases.persona: First-time buyer under listing-agent pressure
cases.deal: Listing agent tells buyer the inspection is informational only and asks them to sign off immediately.
findings: boiler leaks at pressure relief valve
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not sign off just because the listing side pressures you; evaluate boiler and panel safety with your agent before releasing contingency.

cases.sourceBasis: Operational packet QA should catch missing source evidence, deadline risk, loan-type risk, and buyer-message clarity.
cases.persona: Team lead validating product output for launch readiness
cases.deal: Synthetic cross-state QA case for whether the product produces complete packet signals.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The packet is not ready until evidence, deadline, and loan type are captured, and the message avoids legal conclusions.

cases.sourceBasis: Across public sources, strong inspection asks are narrow, evidenced, deadline-aware, lender-aware, and separated from cosmetic or maintenance items.
cases.persona: Operations persona regression test for repeat-use buyer-agent workflow
cases.deal: Agent uploads a mixed report and needs a final send/no-send recommendation in a busy transaction pipeline.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not send yet: confirm credit usability and buyer approval, then send a narrow request for roof and electrical safety only.
